from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Lifeguard's Dilemma", [
            "A lifeguard must reach a swimmer as fast as possible.",
            "Running on sand is faster than swimming in water.",
            "The quickest path isn't straight, but Fermat's way."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Draw background: sand (top half) and water (bottom half)
        # The grid rows A-C are sand, D-F are water. Midpoint is between C and D.
        sand_bg = Rectangle(width=5, height=3, fill_color="#C2B280", fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(sand_bg, 'A1', 'C6')
        
        water_bg = Rectangle(width=5, height=3, fill_color="#0077BE", fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(water_bg, 'D1', 'F6')
        
        # Place Point L (Lifeguard) at top-left and Point S (Swimmer) at bottom-right
        dot_l = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_l, 'A1')
        label_l = Text("L", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        label_l.next_to(dot_l, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_s = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_s, 'F6')
        label_s = Text("S", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        label_s.next_to(dot_s, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sand_bg), FadeIn(water_bg))
        self.play(Create(dot_l), Write(label_l), Create(dot_s), Write(label_s))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight line 2 with yellow-gold to represent sand speed focus
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Display velocity vector arrows
        v_sand_arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT*0.8, end=RIGHT*0.8, color="#FFD700", buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(v_sand_arrow, 'B3')
        v_sand_label = Text("v_sand", font_size=18, color="#FFD700")
        v_sand_label.next_to(v_sand_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        v_water_arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT*0.4, end=RIGHT*0.4, color="#1E90FF", buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(v_water_arrow, 'E3')
        v_water_label = Text("v_water", font_size=18, color="#1E90FF")
        v_water_label.next_to(v_water_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_sand_arrow), Write(v_sand_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_water_arrow), Write(v_water_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight line 3 with green to represent the optimal path
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Straight path (dashed)
        straight_path = DashedLine(dot_l.get_center(), dot_s.get_center(), color="#888888")
        
        # Bent path (Optimal: spends more time on sand)
        # Interface point is calculated at the boundary between Row C and D (y = -0.3)
        interface_x = self.grid['C5'][0]
        interface_y = (self.grid['C5'][1] + self.grid['D5'][1]) / 2
        interface_point = np.array([interface_x, interface_y, 0])
        
        bent_path = VMobject(color="#00FF00")
        bent_path.set_points_as_corners([dot_l.get_center(), interface_point, dot_s.get_center()])
        
        self.play(Create(straight_path))
        self.play(Create(bent_path), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content - Using Text instead of Tex to avoid LaTeX dependency issues
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=18, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.scale(0.85).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # 6x6 grid on the right side for visualization
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset to the right half of the screen
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Set up the lecture frame
        # Strings modified to remove LaTeX syntax and use Unicode where appropriate
        self.setup_layout(
            "Snell's Law via Fermat's Principle",
            [
                "- Fermat: Light takes path of least time",
                "- Total Time T = L1/v1 + L2/v2",
                "- v = c/n => T = 1/c (n1 L1 + n2 L2)",
                "- Minimize T(x) by setting dT/dx = 0",
                "- Result: n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2"
            ]
        )

        # Optical Interface
        interface = Line(LEFT * 2.5, RIGHT * 2.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(interface, "C3")
        interface.shift(RIGHT * 0.5)

        # Normal Line
        normal = DashedLine(UP * 2, DOWN * 2, color=GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(normal, "C3")
        normal.shift(RIGHT * 0.5)

        # Calculation of hit point based on grid
        hit_point = self.grid["C3"] + RIGHT * 0.5
        
        # Rays
        start_point = hit_point + LEFT * 1.5 + UP * 1.8
        end_point = hit_point + RIGHT * 1.2 + DOWN * 1.8
        
        incident_ray = Line(start_point, hit_point, color=YELLOW)
        refracted_ray = Line(hit_point, end_point, color=YELLOW)

        # Labels (Converted from MathTex to Text)
        n1_label = Text("n1", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(n1_label, "B5", 0.8)
        
        n2_label = Text("n2", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(n2_label, "E5", 0.8)

        # Angles (Converted from MathTex to Text)
        theta1 = Text("θ1", font_size=20).move_to(hit_point + UP * 0.7 + LEFT * 0.25)
        theta2 = Text("θ2", font_size=20).move_to(hit_point + DOWN * 0.7 + RIGHT * 0.25)

        # Animations
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=UP))
        self.play(Create(interface), Create(normal))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(incident_ray))
        self.play(Create(refracted_ray))
        self.play(
            Write(n1_label), 
            Write(n2_label),
            Write(theta1),
            Write(theta2)
        )
        
        # Final formula highlight (Converted from MathTex to Text)
        final_formula = Text("n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2", color=YELLOW, font_size=32)
        final_formula.next_to(self.title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        self.play(Write(final_formula))
        
        self.wait(3)

            "Let point A be in air and B in water.",

        self.setup_layout("Geometric Setup of the Boundary", lecture_lines)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Media visualization (Air and Water)

        air_rect = Rectangle(width=5.0, height=2.0, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=BLUE_A, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(air_rect, 'A1', 'C6')
        
        water_rect = Rectangle(width=5.0, height=3.0, fill_opacity=0.2, fill_color=BLUE_E, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(water_rect, 'C1', 'F6')
        
        # Interface line (horizontal through row C)
        interface = Line(self.grid['C1'], self.grid['C6'], color=WHITE)
        
        # Point A at B2 and Point B at E5
        dot_a = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_a, 'B2')
        label_a_pt = Text("A", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00").next_to(dot_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        dot_b = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_b, 'E5')

        self.play(Create(interface))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_a), FadeIn(label_a_pt), FadeIn(dot_b), FadeIn(label_b_pt))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Light hits the interface at a variable point x.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Point P on the interface (C4)
        dot_p = Dot(color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_p, 'C4')
        label_p = Text("P", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF").next_to(dot_p, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Horizontal distance 'x' (from projection of A at C2 to P at C4)

        x_line = Line(self.grid['C2'], self.grid['C4'], color="#00FFFF").shift(DOWN * 0.4)
        label_x = Text("x", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF").next_to(x_line, DOWN, buff=0.05)

        label_a_height = Text("a", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00").next_to(dash_a, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        dash_b = DashedLine(self.grid['E5'], self.grid['C5'], color="#FF00FF")
        label_b_height = Text("b", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF").next_to(dash_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Total horizontal distance d (from projection of A at C2 to projection of B at C5)
        d_line = Line(self.grid['C2'], self.grid['C5'], color=WHITE).shift(DOWN * 1.0)
        label_d = Text("d", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(d_line, DOWN, buff=0.05)

        self.play(Create(dash_b), FadeIn(label_b_height))

outline.topic: Proof of Snell's Law via Fermat's Principle
outline.target_audience: First-year university physics students or advanced high school students

sections.title: The Hook: The Lifeguard's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Least Time' using a relatable analogy. Light doesn't just travel in a way that minimizes distance, but in a way that minimizes time. This sets the conceptual stage for Fermat's Principle without jumping straight into equations.
sections.example: An animation of a lifeguard (Character) on a beach needing to reach a swimmer in the water. The lifeguard runs faster on sand than they swim in water. To reach the swimmer fastest, they shouldn't run in a straight line; they should stay on the sand longer to maximize speed before entering the water.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Index of Refraction
sections.content: Define the relationship between the speed of light in a vacuum (c), the speed in a medium (v), and the refractive index (n). Visualizing light as a wave slowing down and its wavelength shortening helps ground the math.
sections.example: A split-screen graphic showing light moving through air (n=1) vs. water (n=1.33), with a 'speedometer' icon showing v = c/n.

sections.title: Geometric Setup of the Boundary
sections.content: Establish a coordinate system. Place Point A in Medium 1 and Point B in Medium 2. Define the interface as the x-axis. Identify the variables: horizontal distance (d), heights (a and b), and the transition point (x).
sections.example: A clear 2D diagram where a light ray travels from A(0, a) to a point P(x, 0) on the interface, then to B(d, -b). Use bright, contrasting colors for the two media.

sections.title: The Time Equation Construction
sections.content: Using the Pythagorean theorem, express the total travel time (T) as the sum of time spent in Medium 1 and Medium 2. T = (Distance1 / v1) + (Distance2 / v2).
sections.example: The formula T(x) = [sqrt(x² + a²) / v1] + [sqrt((d-x)² + b²) / v2] appears on screen, with the corresponding triangle segments pulsing to show where each term comes from.

sections.title: Calculus: Minimizing the Path
sections.content: Apply Fermat's Principle by finding the derivative of Time (T) with respect to the position (x) and setting it to zero (dT/dx = 0). This identifies the point of 'Least Time'.
sections.example: A step-by-step calculus animation showing the power rule and chain rule application. The derivative results in: [x / (v1 * sqrt(x² + a²))] - [(d-x) / (v2 * sqrt((d-x)² + b²))] = 0.

sections.title: The Geometric Substitution
sections.content: Link the algebraic derivative back to the physical angles of incidence (θ1) and refraction (θ2). Show that x/L1 is sin(θ1) and (d-x)/L2 is sin(θ2).
sections.example: Superimpose 'sin(θ1)' and 'sin(θ2)' over the corresponding ratios in the equation. The equation simplifies to: sin(θ1) / v1 = sin(θ2) / v2.

sections.title: The Final Reveal: Snell's Law
sections.content: Replace the velocities (v) with (c/n). The 'c' terms cancel out, leaving the final, elegant form of Snell's Law.
sections.example: The final transition: (n1 * sin(θ1)) / c = (n2 * sin(θ2)) / c, leading to the glowing conclusion: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Use an Archer fish (Animal) aiming at a bug as a real-world application of this math in nature.

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Lifeguard's Dilemma
lecture_lines: A lifeguard must reach a swimmer as fast as possible.
Running on sand is faster than swimming in water.
The quickest path isn't straight, but Fermat's way.
animations: Draw background: top half #C2B280 (sand), bottom half #0077BE (water). Place Point L (#FFFFFF) at top-left and Point S (#FFFFFF) at bottom-right.
Display vector arrow in sand labeled 'v_sand' (#FFD700) and a shorter vector arrow in water labeled 'v_water' (#1E90FF).
Draw a straight dashed line from L to S (#888888). Overlay a solid path (#00FF00) that bends at the interface to spend more distance on sand.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Index of Refraction
lecture_lines: Light travels slower in dense media like water.
The index of refraction, n, defines this speed reduction.
Speed v equals speed of light c divided by n.
animations: Draw horizontal white line (#FFFFFF). Color upper region light blue (#87CEEB) and lower region cyan (#E0FFFF). Light ray (yellow #FFFF00) enters from top.
Label upper region 'n1' and lower region 'n2' (#FFFFFF). Display text 'n2 > n1' indicating higher density.
Display equation 'v = c / n' (#00FF00) in a central box. Highlight 'v' and 'n' as inversely proportional.

storyboard.title: Geometric Setup of the Boundary
lecture_lines: Let point A be in air and B in water.
Light hits the interface at a variable point x.
Vertical heights are a and b; horizontal distance is d.
Path L1 connects point A to the interface.
Path L2 connects the interface to point B.
animations: Draw horizontal line (#FFFFFF). Place Point A (#FFFF00) at (0, a) and Point B (#FF00FF) at (d, -b).
Place point P (#00FFFF) on the interface. Label the horizontal distance from the origin to P as 'x'.
Draw dashed vertical lines from A and B to the interface. Label heights 'a' (#FFFF00) and 'b' (#FF00FF). Label total width 'd' (#FFFFFF).
Draw solid line segment from A to P and label it 'L1' (#FFFF00).
Draw solid line segment from P to B and label it 'L2' (#FF00FF).

storyboard.title: The Time Equation Construction
lecture_lines: Total time is distance divided by speed in each medium.
We use Pythagoras to find lengths L1 and L2.
Time T(x) equals L1/v1 plus L2/v2.
animations: Display formula 'Time = Distance / Speed' (#00FF00) at top.
Show equations 'L1 = sqrt(x^2 + a^2)' (#FFFF00) and 'L2 = sqrt((d-x)^2 + b^2)' (#FF00FF) near their respective triangles.
Write 'T(x) = L1/v1 + L2/v2' (#00FF00) at the bottom, substituting the square root expressions.

storyboard.title: Calculus: Minimizing the Path
lecture_lines: Fermat's Principle states light minimizes the travel time.
We find the derivative of T with respect to x.
Setting the derivative to zero finds the minimum time.
Apply the chain rule to the square root terms.
This gives the equilibrium condition for the path.
animations: Display 'Fermat: dT/dx = 0' (#FFD700) in center screen.
Write the full derivative expression for T(x) with respect to x using the square root terms (#FFFFFF).
Show the derivative set to zero: '1/v1 * d/dx(L1) + 1/v2 * d/dx(L2) = 0' (#FFFFFF).
Perform calculus step: 'x / (v1 * sqrt(x^2+a^2)) - (d-x) / (v2 * sqrt((d-x)^2+b^2)) = 0' (#FFFFFF).
Simplify to equilibrium condition: 'x / (v1 * L1) = (d-x) / (v2 * L2)' (#00FF00).

storyboard.title: The Geometric Substitution
lecture_lines: Look at the triangles formed by the light path.
The ratio x over L1 is sin(theta 1).
Ratio (d minus x) over L2 is sin(theta 2).
Substitute these sines into our derivative equation.
We get sin(theta 1)/v1 equals sin(theta 2)/v2.
animations: Focus on the geometry. Highlight angle theta1 (#FFFF00) at Point A and theta2 (#FF00FF) at Point B relative to the normal.
Display 'sin(theta1) = x / L1' (#FFFF00) next to the first triangle.
Display 'sin(theta2) = (d-x) / L2' (#FF00FF) next to the second triangle.
Identify the terms 'x/L1' and '(d-x)/L2' in the previous derivative equation: '(1/v1) * (x/L1) = (1/v2) * ((d-x)/L2)'.
Substitute sines to get 'sin(theta1) / v1 = sin(theta2) / v2' (#00FF00).

storyboard.title: The Final Reveal: Snell's Law
lecture_lines: Replace speeds v with c over refractive index n.
The constant speed of light c cancels out.
Result: n1 sin(theta 1) equals n2 sin(theta 2).
animations: Substitute v1 = c/n1 and v2 = c/n2 into the equation to get '(sin(theta1))/(c/n1) = (sin(theta2))/(c/n2)' (#FFFFFF).
Rewrite as '(n1 * sin(theta1)) / c = (n2 * sin(theta2)) / c'. Strike through the 'c' terms with red lines (#FF0000).
Display final law: 'n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2)' in large, glowing gold text (#FFD700).
